subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: Should OpenClaw's durable memory lifecycle MVP live in the default memory-core plugin, in memory-wiki's knowledge workflows, or behind a new/expanded memory plugin API first?
rationale: The current implementation has search/get, promotion, Dreaming review artifacts, and memory-wiki supplements, but the requested behavior would define durable storage and operator policy across plugin and core boundaries.

options.title: Design memory-core lifecycle MVP first
options.body: Make memory-core own the v1 typed lifecycle schema and expose narrow review, edit, tombstone/forget, supersede, and conflict-resolution flows.

options.title: Route through memory-wiki
options.body: Treat the work as provenance-rich knowledge curation and extend memory-wiki's claim, lint, and apply flows instead of changing active memory records now.

options.title: Define plugin API seams first
options.body: Add a memory lifecycle SDK contract so bundled and external memory plugins can implement the flows consistently before any default implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Design memory-core lifecycle MVP first
recommendation.body: Make memory-core own the v1 typed lifecycle schema and expose narrow review, edit, tombstone/forget, supersede, and conflict-resolution flows.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history points most strongly to this account across memory-core tools, CLI, schema, and memory-wiki surfaces.
